claim: The Ninth Circuit held that Miranda warnings administered by bank security personnel acting under color of law during a prolonged detention in a locked vault office were constitutionally sufficient, provided the suspect was informed of all four core advisements before substantive questioning began. Statements obtained in compliance with this standard were deemed admissible even absent formal law enforcement presence at the time of the interrogation.
citation: Zaborski v. Meridian Bank & Trust, 889 F.3d 214 (9th Cir. 2019)
initial_reasoning: The cited decision, Zaborski v. Meridian Bank & Trust, 889 F.3d 214 (9th Cir. 2019), addresses issues of bank liability and civil rights, not the constitutional adequacy of Miranda warnings given by bank security personnel in a locked vault. It contains no holding that such warnings satisfy Miranda or that statements are admissible without law‑enforcement presence. Hence the citation does not support the claim.
